follow-up time: Until birth or termination of pregnancy
outcome: Prenatal diagnosis of fetal abdominal defects
Pregnancy outcomes (missed abortion, termination, live birth)
finding: Prenatal diagnosis of fetal abdominal wall defects is important due to the varying perinatal and neonatal morbidity and mortality associated with different types of defects, underlying chromosomal abnormalities, and associated structural anomalies.
mod_finding: Expectant management with cesarean delivery between 38-39 gestational weeks was performed in three cases of gastroschisis.
cohort: 27 cases diagnosed with fetal abdominal wall defects between January 2011 and February 2014 at Celal Bayar University, Manisa, Turkey
